clips.title: Build & deploy agents with the Claude Agent SDK
clips.why: A tour of the SDK's core primitives, ending with permissions, so you see where tools and permissions sit among the other options.
look: Which primitives he lists, and how permissions sit next to tools rather than inside them.
That permissions are configured in code, before the session starts.
clips.after: Our sessions decide every permission in the options object, because nobody watches a VM.

clips.title: Claude Code Permissions Explained: Why Your Allow Rule Still Fails
clips.why: The order of the checks in under two minutes: deny first, then ask, then allow.
look: Why a deny rule beats an allow rule even when the allow rule is more specific.
Where ask rules sit, and why that matters when nobody can answer.
clips.after: The same order runs in every agent session, with hooks before it and dontAsk turning every unanswered question into a refusal.

clips.title: Claude Code Permissions Explained: Why Your Allow Rule Still Fails
clips.why: The permission modes one by one, and what bypassPermissions really lets through.
look: How each mode answers a call that no rule settled.
The part on bypassPermissions: everything is approved, and an allow list does not narrow it.
clips.after: This is exactly how the reviewer in the story edited a test file, and why we use dontAsk.

practice.q: You want the model to never see WebFetch at all, so it does not waste a turn trying it. Which option does that?

options.why: WebFetch would still exist, and the model may try it and be refused.
A plain name in disallowedTools removes the tool from the request, so the model never knows it existed.
A scoped rule leaves the tool installed and denies matching calls. The model can still waste a turn on it.

practice.q: Finish the options so that any call not approved in advance is denied, without asking anyone.
practice.hint: Two words joined together: do not ask.
practice.why: dontAsk never prompts and denies anything not pre-approved, which is what a session with nobody watching needs.

practice.q: Put the permission checks in the order the SDK runs them for one tool call.
practice.why: Hooks run first and a deny anywhere wins. dontAsk skips the last step and denies instead.

practice.q: Write the allow rule that lets a session run the test script and no other shell command.
practice.hint: The tool name, then the command pattern in brackets.
practice.why: A scoped rule approves only matching calls. Every other Bash call goes to the permission mode, where dontAsk denies it.

practice.q: You want to stop every write to secrets/ in the working folder, by Edit and by Write. Which deny rule do you add?

options.why: A Write(path) rule is never matched by the file checks. File rules are written with Edit.
One Edit rule covers every built-in tool that writes files, and a single slash is relative to the working folder.
Two slashes mean the absolute path /secrets on disk, not the folder inside your project.
